model.description:
The pricing pairing: one catalogue Bedrock model id, re-resolved on every read so a
catalogue refresh reprices the entry and an id that has left the catalogue stays saved
(FR-034a.1, FR-034a.3).

name.description: Shown instead of the profile id when set (FR-026).

oneOf.description:
A hand-entered cost, in the catalogue's per-million rates; set means no catalogue lookup
happens and a refresh never overwrites it (FR-034a.4).

tool_call.description: Whether the profile takes tools; unset is unknown.

ProfileEntryResponse.description:
One saved inference-profile entry as the settings row shows it (contracts §4): the ARN the
person pasted, the limits they set, the optional pricing pairing, and a name to show for it.

context.description:
Unknown when unset — never "unsupported", never copied from the paired model (FR-028,
FR-034a.6).

display_name.description: The entry's name, or the profile id from its ARN when it has none (FR-026).

oneOf.description:
Which of the two limits the person set by hand, so a re-pairing refreshes only the others
(FR-034a.7). Server-owned: the client never sets it, and `null` on an entry saved before
this rule reads as "true wherever a number is present".

model.description: The catalogue model id the entry is priced from, when the person paired one (FR-034a.1).

oneOf.description: The hand-entered cost, when there is one (FR-034a.4).

pricing.description:
What its usage will cost right now, computed from the entry's current state — the figure,
or the absence with a cause-specific reason and the way out (contracts §4a, FR-034a.2,
FR-034a.3, FR-034b, SC-021). Never stored, so re-picking a model or entering a price
clears it with no manual edit.

worktree_count.description: Worktree chats whose folders stay on disk when the project is removed (FR-033).

ProjectMode.description:
What a project chat may do (`specs/041-project-coding-workspace` FR-009): Plan is read-only,
Build may change files and, with the shell switch on, run commands. No row means `Plan`.

ProjectScope.description:
The project a subagent piece works in, copied from the launching turn (FR-007a). Set only
by `BackgroundJobs::dispatch_piece`, never by a client.

mode.description: The launching turn's mode, fixed for the piece.

topic.description: The launching chat's topic: resolves its worktree.

last_activity.description: Unix milliseconds; `null` for a brand-new empty session.

oneOf.description: The worktree this chat works in, when it has one.

ProjectSkillRow.description: One skill a project chat can run, as the composer's `/` menu lists it.

argument_hint.description: The usage line the skill declares, e.g. `[audit|critique] [target]`.

folder.description: Its folder relative to the chat's folder, which is what `use_skill` reports.

scope.description:
`project`. Every row here is one, and saying so keeps the shape the same if a later route
merges the workspace scopes in.

user_invocable.description: Whether a person may run it by name; a `false` one is prose for the agent, not a command.

folder.description: The canonical folder, with Windows' `\\?\` prefix stripped for display.

session_count.description: Sessions in the project across every owner (the sidebar's project row).

ProviderGuide.description: What the connect form shows above the fields. Static metadata, never stored or editable.

ProviderId.description: A provider id: a catalogue provider, a built-in or a custom provider

ProviderResponse.description: A connected provider: saved credentials or a key in the environment, never the secrets.

access_key_id.description: AWS Bedrock: the access key id is an identifier, not a secret.

has_sso_session.description: A session row exists and decrypts with this workspace key.

migrated_from.description: The pre-015 name this provider's saved row was migrated from.

profiles.description: The saved inference-profile entries, as saved: no price is invented here (FR-026, FR-028).

reachable.description: Local and custom providers only; checked in the background.

role_name.description: The role chosen from the portal.

session_expires_at.description: When the stored session's access token expires.

session_failure.description:
What the connection last failed with, when that failure was about the session itself —
a session revoked in AWS while its token still looked valid, for instance (FR-016,
FR-018). Cleared by the next successful sign-in, which needs no Vizier restart.

source.description: `saved`, `env:NAME`, or `null` for a local provider on its default address.

sso_profile.description: The non-secret handle the session is stored under (FR-009e).

sso_region.description: The Identity Center's region — not the Bedrock region (FR-010).

oneOf.description: `configured`, `signed-in`, `expired` or `unreadable`; `null` for every other provider.

start_url.description: The Identity Center start URL, shown in clear (FR-009b).

variant.description: The same id, under the field name pre-015 clients read.

endpoint.description: Where requests go by default (may hold `${VAR}`); custom providers: their base URL.

oneOf.description: The in-form setup guide, when this provider has one (Amazon Bedrock today).

logo_full_color.description: The logo has its own colours; don't invert it on a dark theme.

popular.description: One of the providers vizier supported before the catalogue.

Question.description:
One question in a set (FR-002, FR-003).

The type-specific fields are flat, as the wire contract states them, and
[`crate::questions::validate`] is the one place that decides which apply to which type: a
`choice` with no `options` is refused, and `max_length` on a `choice` is ignored rather than
rejected, so an agent that sends a superset still gets a usable question.

oneOf.description: Counts as an answer, so a required question with a default may be submitted untouched.

help.description: Shown under the prompt, for a question whose point is not obvious.

id.description: Stable within the set; what the answer names.

max_length.description: `text`: the longest answer accepted, in bytes.

max_selections.description: `multi_choice`: the most answers accepted. Defaults to every option.

min_selections.description: `multi_choice`: the fewest answers accepted. Defaults to none.

multiline.description: `text`: a roomier field, for an answer that is a sentence or more.

no_label.description: `confirm`: the label of the negative button.

optional.description: Required by default; an optional question may be left blank and arrives as `skipped`.

placeholder.description: `text`: a hint shown in an empty field.

prompt.description: The question itself, shown as the field's label.

yes_label.description: `confirm`: the label of the affirmative button.

QuestionAnswer.description: The person's answer, carried as a turn of its own (`contracts/questions-wire.md` §7).

answerer.description: Who submitted it, as the surface identifies them.

answers.description: One entry per question, in the set's order.

declined.description: The person dismissed the set instead of answering it (FR-014).

text.description:
What the conversation shows as the person's message. Built at submission when the client
does not supply one.

QuestionType.description: What kind of answer a question wants (FR-003).

Rank.description: How agents are ordered when there are more rows than the grid shows.

message_uid.description: The history uid of an agent's reply in this topic.

RecallOrigin.description: How recalled passages reached the turn.

state.description: Never `Running`/`Interrupted`; `Cancelled` only in a cancel's tool result.

text.description: The answer (truncated) or the reason it did not answer.

oneOf.description:
Someone asked for this task, identified as the channel they reached the
agent on knows them — `"@dani (DiscordId: 182…)"`, a web username.

user.description:
Someone asked for this task, identified as the channel they reached the
agent on knows them — `"@dani (DiscordId: 182…)"`, a web username.

oneOf.description: The agent set this task up itself, with no one asking.

agent.description: The agent set this task up itself, with no one asking.

Requester.description:
Who wanted a task to exist.

The one distinction that matters — somebody asked, versus the agent set this
up on its own initiative — made unforgeable in the type. `User`'s payload is
deliberately not an account: most people reaching an agent have none, and the
chat channels already synthesise an identity string for them.

root.description: A root already listed, relative to the project folder; without it every root restarts.

RoleItem.description: A role with how many people have it.

RoleList.description: The role list, with the same fallback rule as [`AccountList`].

RoleView.description: One role the identity may assume in an account.

no_change.description:
`true` when the restored content was already identical to the current one, so no new
revision was appended.

before.description: `ran_at` of the oldest run on the previous page.

before_id.description:
That run's `id`, completing the cursor so runs sharing a millisecond cannot
straddle a page boundary. Ignored without `before`.

oneOf.description:
RFC 3339 with an offset is that exact moment; a date and time with no offset
(`2026-11-07T09:00`) is the instance's local time.

SecretItem.description: One secret as a person sees it: its name, the server's mask, and who changed it when.

masked.description: `utils::mask_secret` of the stored value. There is no field for the value itself.

updated_by_name.description: The username or the agent's name; the id when it cannot be resolved.

counts.description: With `limit`: matches per filter key (`all`). Always carries `all`.

ServerOverride.description: A person's choice of server for one language in one project (`data-model.md` §2).

ServerStatus.description: What the sign-in page needs before anyone has signed in.

setup_required.description: No one has been set up yet: show Onboarding.

history_uid.description: The request entry the file arrived with, when it was attached to one.

sender.description: Who the file came from: a person's username, or the agent id.

seq.description:
Explicit ordering position within the agent's history, breaking the ties that
`timestamp` alone leaves ambiguous — a turn's entries are all flushed in one tight
loop, so sharing a millisecond is the normal case.

Assigned by the storage layer on insert and never by a caller. `None` means the entry
was recorded before the column existed; such entries are not retroactively ordered
(`specs/010-webui-reasoning-display`, FR-006/FR-007). It lives on the row rather than
inside the serialized `data` blob, so reads read it from the column.

oneOf.description:
A call the agent made to a tool the person's client declared
(`specs/019-client-tools`), saved when it is made. The entry's uid is the call id.
`outcome` and `state` change after the insert, so they live in `client_tool_call`
and are filled in on every read, never written into the stored blob.

ClientToolCall.description:
A call the agent made to a tool the person's client declared
(`specs/019-client-tools`), saved when it is made. The entry's uid is the call id.
`outcome` and `state` change after the insert, so they live in `client_tool_call`
and are filled in on every read, never written into the stored blob.

oneOf.description:
Memory passages the agent was given or went looking for during a turn
(`specs/024-webui-rewrite`, FR-018e). Display only: never part of the model's input.

Recall.description:
Memory passages the agent was given or went looking for during a turn
(`specs/024-webui-rewrite`, FR-018e). Display only: never part of the model's input.

oneOf.description:
A question set the agent asked (`specs/042-agent-asking-question`), saved when it is
presented. Its uid **is** the set id. `state`, `answers` and `answerer` change after the
insert, so they live in `question_set` and are filled in on every read, exactly as
`ClientToolCall`'s `outcome` and `state` are.

QuestionSet.description:
A question set the agent asked (`specs/042-agent-asking-question`), saved when it is
presented. Its uid **is** the set id. `state`, `answers` and `answerer` change after the
insert, so they live in `question_set` and are filled in on every read, exactly as
`ClientToolCall`'s `outcome` and `state` are.

oneOf.description:
An ask for a sensitive value (`specs/042-agent-asking-question`). Says that one was
requested, why, and what came of it — **never the value** (FR-044, FR-054). Its `state` is
filled at read time from `sensitive_ask`.

SensitiveAsk.description:
An ask for a sensitive value (`specs/042-agent-asking-question`). Says that one was
requested, why, and what came of it — **never the value** (FR-044, FR-054). Its `state` is
filled at read time from `sensitive_ask`.

value.description: The value to store. Never returned by any route.

SetupPhase.description: Where an agent's setup currently is.

SetupState.description: One agent's setup, as the WebUI sees it.

name.description:
The agent's display name from the build's config; a create build is not in the agent
store yet, so the panel cannot always resolve it.

ShareListItem.description: A share item in a list (`GET /shares`).

title.description:
Withheld (absent) in the administrator's list for a share whose audience does not
include the administrator (FR-043): the title comes from the conversation.

ShareView.description:
A share as `GET /shares/{id}` returns it. No field depends on who asks, and the audience
kind is not among them (FR-030): a reader is not told who else can read.

SideChat.description:
One `/btw` side chat carried in each request: the question being asked now and the
aside's earlier turns, held between asks only by whoever shows the side chat (the WebUI
panel, or a Discord/Telegram reader). Never stored.

SignInProgress.description: What a poll of the pending sign-in answered: still waiting (`202`), or signed in (`200`).

SignInRequest.description:
What the form is about to save for one connection. Every field is optional; an omitted value
falls back to the saved row, so a saved connection starts a re-sign-in with an empty body
(FR-008).

profile.description: The profile name the session is stored under (FR-009e).

SignInResponse.description:
One answer to `POST /{id}/sso/sign-in` (contracts §3): a fresh code to type, the pending state
after a poll, or the completed sign-in. Untagged on the wire, exactly the three bodies the
contract shows — and none of them carries the device code, a token or a secret half (FR-009b).

SignInStarted.description: The pending panel: the code and the URL, and never the device code (contracts §3).

SignOutResponse.description: After a sign-out the connection is configured and has no session; nothing else changed.

agents.description: The member agents that have it.

SsoSessionState.description:
Where the connection stands, as the settings row renders it (data-model "the connection
state machine"). Derived from the stored rows on every read, never stored itself.

entry.description: A history entry in the shape `GET …/history` returns.

oneOf.description:
`null` for a task that has never run — distinct from a run that answered nothing,
which is a `last_run` whose `response` is `null`.

next_run.description:
When it runs next: a cron task's next occurrence, a one-time task's moment while it is
still ahead; `null` when inactive or finished.

TaskRunResponse.description:
One run as the task screen reads it.

`response` is `Some` only on the detail route, where the response is what a person came
to read. The listing and the task list leave it `None`, so neither can spend a page of
JSON on text nobody asked for.

response.description: Absent on the listing routes; `null` for a run that answered nothing.

run_id.description: The run's address — its `ran_at` — which the detail routes take.

TaskRunState.description:
Terminal states are terminal — nothing re-opens a closed run. *Not yet run*
is the **absence** of rows for a task, not a state.

`Answered` means the agent produced a response, not that the news was good: a
run whose response reports a failure is still `Answered`.

has_more.description: FR-009: a caller must not be offered a page that does not exist.

billing.description:
The marker of one billable inference call. Set only when the test really invoked a model —
the SSO test spends exactly one call (FR-012a, SC-018) — and never by a listing or a
failure, which spend nothing.

model.description:
The target the test invoked, when the test is a real call: the SSO provider's test proves
one model or inference profile, so it names it (contract `media-and-test.md` §1).

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the page above; none when there is nothing older.

steps.description: What the member agents did in the same span, to merge with `entries` by time.

running_jobs.description: Background jobs launched from this topic that are still in flight.

unread.description: Messages from others the person has not read in this topic.

base_seq.description:
The revision this edit started from (`seq` of `GET /core`). When the identity document
has moved on, the save is refused with `409 stale_revision` instead of overwriting the
newer text.

The revision this edit started from, when the client knows it. When the document has
moved on, the save is refused with `409 stale_revision` and the newer content instead of
overwriting it (FR-028). Optional and additive: a client that omits it keeps the old
last-write-wins behaviour.

warning.description: Present only when the content went over the soft limit (contracts/http-api.md).

lsp_enabled.description: Language servers on or off (`specs/054-project-lsp`). Off stops them at once.

UpsertProviderRequest.description: Credentials to save. An omitted field keeps the stored value; an empty string clears it.

model.description:
The target of a **Test** on the SSO provider: the model id or inference-profile ARN to
invoke (contract `media-and-test.md` §1). Upsert ignores it — it is not a credential, so it
is deliberately absent from [`Self::sent`] and [`Self::into_credentials`], and saving
neither stores nor clears anything for it.

profiles.description:
Amazon Bedrock (SSO): the whole inference-profile list, one operation — omitted keeps the
stored list, `[]` clears it (FR-021).

region.description: AWS region; for the SSO provider this is the **Bedrock** region (FR-010).

role_name.description: Amazon Bedrock (SSO): the role chosen from the portal.

secret_access_key.description: AWS Bedrock secret access key (write-only after saving).

session_token.description: AWS Bedrock temporary-credential session token (write-only after saving).

sso_profile.description: Amazon Bedrock (SSO): the non-secret handle the session is stored under (FR-009e).

sso_region.description:
Amazon Bedrock (SSO): the region the Identity Center instance lives in; defaults from
`region` when only that one is given (FR-010).

start_url.description: Amazon Bedrock (SSO): the Identity Center start URL (FR-005).

UsageActivity.description: What a model call was for. Decided once, when the call is recorded (research R4).

accounting_since.description:
When complete accounting started (R6); ranges before it lack dreams, compaction and
failed rounds.

cost_usd.description: `null` (not `0`) when nothing in scope has a known price.

share_of_all.description: Set only when the report is narrowed to one activity: its share of all activities' cost.

UsedBy.description: Agents per feature using one provider's credentials. Dream and read-image count as chat.

oneOf.description:
An artifact by identity (`specs/035-add-artifacts`). The bytes are resolved through an
[`AttachmentResolver`]; `available` is read-time only and never stored.

artifact.description:
An artifact by identity (`specs/035-add-artifacts`). The bytes are resolved through an
[`AttachmentResolver`]; `available` is read-time only and never stored.

background_depth.description:
How many background hops led to this turn: 0 for anything a person or the scheduler
started, `job.depth + 1` for a background piece or a background report. Carried on the
request rather than the session, because a woken turn runs in the same session as the
turn that launched the job and must still count as one level deeper.

client_context.description:
What the client that sent this request says about itself: what it renders, what it
offers, how it is being used. The WebUI says it draws mermaid diagrams and LaTeX.

A note for the turn that sent it. It is rendered into the turn's context block
(`system_prompt::context::client_context_note`) and deliberately left out of
[`VizierRequest::to_prompt`]: the block rides the newest user message and is never
stored, so a replayed request cannot restate a note from a client that may have gone,
and no later turn inherits it in the person's voice. It stays on the stored request so
a resumed turn rebuilds the same block.

mentions.description:
Files and folders a project chat's message mentions (FR-018). Their contents are
resolved when the turn starts and never stored.

oneOf.description: Explicit provider/model for this chat turn; absent means the configured agent model.

The project a subagent piece works in (`specs/041-project-coding-workspace` R11),
copied from the launching turn by `BackgroundJobs::dispatch_piece`. It is serialised
with the durable turn row, so a resumed piece keeps the folder and mode it started
with; clients cannot send it.

scheduled_task.description:
The slug of the task this request is a scheduled run of.

Set by the scheduler and by nothing else, which is what makes it safe where the
request content kind is not: the dream cycle sends `Unattended` too and must not be
attributed to the scheduler. `Default` leaves it `None` for every other construction
site, so no interactive turn's frontmatter changes.

oneOf.description:
A machine wrote this prompt and nobody is waiting on the answer — a
scheduled task run, or a dream cycle's own work. Deliberately not named
`Task`: two of its three construction sites are the dream cycle, and the
old name invited selecting scheduled-run behaviour on the content kind
rather than on the session's channel.

unattended.description:
A machine wrote this prompt and nobody is waiting on the answer — a
scheduled task run, or a dream cycle's own work. Deliberately not named
`Task`: two of its three construction sites are the dream cycle, and the
old name invited selecting scheduled-run behaviour on the content kind
rather than on the session's channel.

oneOf.description:
The outcome of background work this conversation started (`background_subagents`,
`delegate_agent`), delivered as a turn of its own. Not a message from a person.

background_report.description:
The outcome of background work this conversation started (`background_subagents`,
`delegate_agent`), delivered as a turn of its own. Not a message from a person.

oneOf.description:
A message a client sent on the person's behalf, such as a click inside a page the
agent drew (`specs/019-client-tools`). It starts a turn like `Chat`.

client_event.description:
A message a client sent on the person's behalf, such as a click inside a page the
agent drew (`specs/019-client-tools`). It starts a turn like `Chat`.

oneOf.description:
An off-the-record `/btw` question (`specs/033-btw-side-chat`): the agent answers it
from the conversation's context, but nothing above, about or around it is saved.
Dispatched beside `checkpoint`/`lobotomy`, never through `handle_request`.

btw.description:
An off-the-record `/btw` question (`specs/033-btw-side-chat`): the agent answers it
from the conversation's context, but nothing above, about or around it is saved.
Dispatched beside `checkpoint`/`lobotomy`, never through `handle_request`.

oneOf.description:
A person's answer to a question set (`specs/042-agent-asking-question`). It starts a turn
like `Chat`: same history, same queue, same attribution, no bypass (FR-015).

question_answer.description:
A person's answer to a question set (`specs/042-agent-asking-question`). It starts a turn
like `Chat`: same history, same queue, same attribution, no bypass (FR-015).

history_uid.description:
The `session_history` uid this response was saved as. Set by whoever saved it,
after the save, so it is never part of the stored `data`.

resumed.description:
The turn was interrupted by a restart and carried on afterwards
(`specs/023-persist-turn-activity`).

depth_exhausted.description: The turn reached `thinking_depth`, and the reply is what it had by then (#48).

ended_by_tool.description: The turn ended because this turn-ending tool succeeded, not because the model answered.

provider.description: The provider and model that answered, for the usage view's cost estimate (FR-021).

role.description: `owner`, `member`, or `admin` for someone who manages every Workspace without being in it.

working.description: An agent is working in it.

WorktreeSummary.description: A worktree as the sidebar and a create response show it.

Zone.description: The instance's timezone, as reported to clients and the startup log.

name.description: IANA name, such as `Asia/Jakarta`. `None` only when the host's zone cannot be named.

offset.description:
The current offset, such as `+07:00`. It changes with daylight saving, so it is computed
on every read.
